title: Hasty Ordinations and Expelled Monks
english: …bishops; and since perhaps no one reports their circumstances, they are ordained clerics, or even presbyters.
2. On those who leave monasteries and are ordained

Others, expelled as disorderly from the monasteries themselves, then slip in to obtain ordination; and once they have become clerics, they enter even the very monasteries from which they were expelled, and wish to make the offering and to perform all that clerics are accustomed to do. And they do this, so that some who know them even stay away from the assemblies and cannot bear to share in communion while those men are officiating.
translator_notes: Copy-text: the Greek text printed in PG 77. The page marker 283, which falls inside παραιτεῖσθαι, is omitted.
The section opens mid-sentence; the subject ('some who have just married') and verb 'sweep along' stand at the end of the previous section, hence the opening ellipsis.
τάχα που: rendered 'perhaps'.
ἢ γοῦν πρεσβύτεροι: γοῦν stresses the higher grade; rendered 'or even presbyters'.
ὑποτρέχουσι τὰς χειροτονίας: 'run in under, creep in for ordinations'; rendered 'slip in to obtain ordination'. πάλιν is rendered once, as 'then'.
προσφέρειν: the eucharistic offering; rendered 'make the offering' without adding a noun the Greek lacks.

καὶ ταῦτα δρᾶν, ὡς...: the infinitive continues the report of what these men do; ὡς marks the result. Rendered 'they do this, so that...'. παραιτεῖσθαι καὶ τὰς συνάξεις: 'decline even the assemblies'; rendered 'even stay away from the assemblies'.
κοινωνεῖν λειτουργούντων ἐκείνων: 'to communicate while those men officiate'; rendered 'share in communion while those men are officiating'.
Heading '2.' renders the edition's (β) heading.
baehrens: PG 77; Ad episcopos Libyae et Pentapoleos ep rem early

title: Examining Candidates Before Ordination
english: 3. How and when one should ordain, and whom one should examine

Since, then, as I said, everything we do must be done for building up the people, let Your Reverence watch over these matters. If anyone is about to be ordained a cleric, let Your Reverence look carefully into his life: whether he has a wife or not, how or when he married her, and whether he has abstained; and whether he is one of those who have been expelled, either by another most God-fearing bishop or from monasteries. And then let Your Reverence ordain him, once he has been found blameless.
translator_notes: Copy-text: the Greek text printed in PG 77.
ἡ θεοσέβεια ὑμῶν: an honorific address ('your godliness'); rendered 'Your Reverence'. The plural ὑμῶν addresses the bishops together.
The third-person imperatives περιεργαζέσθω and χειροτονείτω carry on the subject ἡ θεοσέβεια ὑμῶν, so 'Your Reverence' is repeated as their subject rather than supplying a new one.
ἠγάγετο: 'took (a wife)'; rendered 'married her'.
εἰ ἀπέσχετο: 'whether he abstained', most likely from marital relations, in line with the concern about men just married; rendered 'whether he has abstained' to keep the Greek's reticence.
εἰ μή τίς ἐστι τῶν ἐκβεβλημένων: indirect question with μή, 'whether he is perhaps one of the expelled' (the check is for exclusion); rendered 'whether he is one of those who have been expelled'.

ἀδιάβλητον εὑρεθέντα: possibly recalls 1 Timothy 3:10 ('let them first be tested; then let them serve if they prove blameless'), but the wording differs (ἀνέγκλητοι there); uncertain, so no inline citation.
Heading '3.' renders the edition's (γ) heading.
baehrens: PG 77; Ad episcopos Libyae et Pentapoleos ep rem mid

title: Catechumens and Penitents Near Death
english: For in this way we shall keep both our own conscience pure and the holy and venerable liturgy beyond reproach.
On catechumens and penitents, if they draw near their end

If any who have been censured for their faults undergo separation, and then are about to die while they are still catechumens, let them be baptized; and let them not depart this life without a share in grace, that is, without communion. For this too seems to be in keeping with the ordinances of the Church.
Greet the brotherhood that is with you; the brotherhood that is with us greets you in the Lord.
translator_notes: Copy-text: the Greek text printed in PG 77. The page marker 284 is omitted.
The section begins a new sentence (the previous section ends at εὑρεθέντα.), so no opening ellipsis. οὕτω ('in this way') refers back to the examination just described.
ἀδιάβλητον: 'blameless, beyond reproach', the same word used of the candidate at the end of the previous section.
The heading 'On catechumens and penitents...' renders the edition's heading (printed 'Ε' in the copy-text); its number is uncertain after (α)-(γ), so no numeral is given.
χωρισμὸν ὑπομείνωσί ... ἐπιτιμηθέντες πταισμάτων ἕνεκα: 'undergo separation, having been censured for faults', i.e. excommunication as a penance; πταίσματα are faults or lapses.
ἤγουν ἀκοινώνητοι: 'that is, without communion'.
δοκεῖ γὰρ προσέχειν καὶ τοῦτο τοῖς τῆς ἐκκλησίας θεσμοῖς: 'for this too seems to keep to the Church's ordinances'.
ὑμᾶς ἡ σὺν ἡμῖν ἐν κυρίῳ προσαγορεύει: subject is ἡ (ἀδελφότης) σὺν ἡμῖν, the brotherhood with Cyril, which greets the bishops; no Scripture citation.
baehrens: PG 77; Ad episcopos Libyae et Pentapoleos ep rem close
